record.paper_title: The Future of Primordial Black Holes: Open Questions and Roadmap
record.context_brief: PBH fraction in observed gravitational-wave events
record.original_question: What fraction, if any, of the binary black-hole gravitational-wave events already observed by LIGO/Virgo/KAGRA should be attributed to primordial black holes rather than astrophysical black-hole formation channels, given that current hierarchical Bayesian analyses can only constrain a putative PBH subpopulation and decisive attribution requires reducing uncertainties in both astrophysical and primordial formation models?

evidence.quote: What fraction of the currently observed GW events can be ascribed to PBHs?

Currently hierarchical Bayesian analysis combining astrophysical formation models and PBHs may only constrain the fraction of a putative subpopulation of PBHs in the data (see for instance Ref. [13]).

The exciting possibility that PBHs are contributing to current observations will be verified only by further reducing uncertainties in astrophysical and primordial formation models. This is another fundamental open issue.

artifact.category_tag: primordial black holes and gravitational-wave populations
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the catalog of binary black-hole merger events detected by current ground-based gravitational-wave observatories operating in the audio-band frequency range (roughly 10 Hz–10 kHz). Each detection provides posterior distributions on source-frame parameters such as component masses, mass ratio, effective spin, redshift, and tidal/eccentricity bounds. Assume two competing population models for the origin of these binaries:

(A) Astrophysical formation channels, in which the black holes are remnants of stellar evolution produced through isolated binary evolution, dynamical assembly in dense stellar environments (e.g. globular clusters, nuclear clusters, AGN disks), chemically homogeneous evolution, or hierarchical mergers; these channels predict mass functions consistent with stellar collapse (with an expected upper mass gap from pulsational pair instability), spin distributions tied to stellar physics, and merger rates evolving with cosmic star formation.

(B) A primordial formation channel, in which the black holes formed in the very early universe (e.g. from the gravitational collapse of large-amplitude cosmological perturbations) and later pair up to merge; this channel predicts a broad mass spectrum extending beyond stellar limits, generically low natal spins, an isotropic spin orientation distribution, and a merger-rate density evolving roughly as (1+z)^{8/3} at high redshift, independent of star formation.

Denote by f_PBH the fraction of the observed binary black-hole gravitational-wave events that originate from channel (B). Using a hierarchical Bayesian population analysis that mixes models (A) and (B) and is conditioned on the full observed catalog (including selection effects), determine f_PBH, or equivalently provide a posterior credible interval for f_PBH and identify which (if any) individual events have a posterior probability greater than 1/2 of being of primordial origin.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent population analyses of LVK O3/O4 catalogs only place upper bounds or weak constraints on a possible PBH subpopulation in the BBH data; no decisive attribution of any specific event to primordial origin has been established, and the fraction remains uncertain due to degeneracies with astrophysical formation models. The question is regarded as open in the gravitational-wave and PBH communities as of 2026.

status_evidence.title: Constraints on primordial black holes from LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA observations
status_evidence.snippet: Hierarchical Bayesian analyses constrain a putative PBH subpopulation in GWTC-3 but cannot conclusively determine the PBH fraction.
status_evidence.claim: Current GW data only constrain, not determine, the PBH fraction among observed BBH events.

status_evidence.title: The Future of Primordial Black Holes: Open Questions and Roadmap
status_evidence.snippet: Identifies the fraction of observed GW events attributable to PBHs as a fundamental open issue requiring reduced modeling uncertainties.
status_evidence.claim: The question is explicitly listed as open.
